test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 27 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: By selling an article for ₹19.50, a dealer makes a profit of 30%. By how much should be increase his selling price so as to make a profit of 40%?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Selling Prices** is proportional to (100 + **Profit%**).

Initial SP : New SP = (100 + 30) : (100 + 40) = 130 : 140 = 13 : 14.

Given 13 units = 19.50 ∴ 1 unit = 19.50 ÷ 13 = 1.50.

The **increase in SP** is (14 − 13) = 1 unit.

Value of 1 unit = 1.50.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1.50.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial SP = 19.50, Initial Profit = 30%, Target Profit = 40%.

**Formulas:** CP = [SP × 100] ÷ [100 + Profit%], New SP = CP × [100 + New Profit%] ÷ 100.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cb7fd400b36eb86f2b8917a8802cf8149f6c987ba981c95a908dcf586dbc67da.png] 

⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** = (19.50 × 100) ÷ 130 = 1950 ÷ 130 = 15.

⇒ **New Selling Price** = 15 × (140 ÷ 100) = 15 × 1.4 = 21.

⇒ **Increase in SP** = New SP − Old SP = 21 − 19.50 = 1.50.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1.50.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price & Selling Price Relationship

When **Cost Price** is constant, the ratio of any two **Selling Prices** is equal to the ratio of their respective (100 ± Profit/Loss%).

Profit Calculation

Profit is always calculated on the **Cost Price** unless specified otherwise. Profit = SP − CP.

20
